problem_statement: The Cinder & Rail project is a small static editorial newsroom (leogodoyllg News-Website-Template) for an independent transit paper, with a sticky masthead, a Green Line showcase hero, an 'Editors Picks' grid of seven story cards across the Transit / Infrastructure / Culture beats, a full article page (article.html), an About page (about.html), and a shared four-column footer. Grow the newsroom's reader-signal idea into a shared design-system component: (1) add a 'Reader signal controls' filter panel above the Editors Picks grid on the home page that narrows the story cards by beat (All stories / Transit / Infrastructure / Culture), and (2) add a shared 'Reader signal rail' to the site FOOTER of EVERY page (home, about, article) so readers can jump to a beat from anywhere. The rail must appear consistently on all three pages. Keep the on-page filter wired end to end: clicking a beat chip (Transit / Infrastructure) must update the 'Showing N stories' status readout to reflect the selected beat (e.g. clicking Transit sets 'Showing 3 stories: night buses, the ferry crossing, and fare-capping.'), not merely highlight the chip and hide cards. The filter panel and rail must keep the Cinder & Rail red/charcoal editorial look (white cards, #c72727 red accent, dark #333 footer, condensed headline type) matching the reference design, and must be responsive so the home page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport. Preserve the Cinder & Rail identity, navigation, hero, Editors Picks cards, local imagery, article page, and the desktop/tablet layout.
required_content: Add the reader-signal filter panel (eyebrow 'READER SIGNAL FILTER', heading 'Reader signal controls', and the four beat chips All stories / Transit / Infrastructure / Culture) above the Editors Picks grid on the home page.

Add the shared 'Reader signal rail' component (eyebrow 'READER SIGNAL RAIL' + beat links) to the FOOTER of ALL THREE pages (home, about, article) so the same reader-signal component appears consistently site-wide, not only on the home page.

Style the filter strip and the shared rail to match the reference Cinder & Rail red/charcoal editorial look (white filter chips with the #c72727 red accent, dark footer rail with the amber #f99500 beat links) -- the rendered filter panel must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette restyle.

Make the filter strip responsive so the home page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport (allow the chips to wrap / use a fluid layout instead of a fixed-width non-wrapping row). Do not merely clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width.
Keep the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts free of horizontal overflow.

Keep the reader-signal filter fully wired end to end: clicking a beat chip (Transit / Infrastructure / All stories) must update the '.signal-status' 'Showing N stories' readout to reflect the selected beat (e.g. clicking Transit yields 'Showing 3 stories: night buses, the ferry crossing, and fare-capping.'), in addition to highlighting the active chip and hiding non-matching cards -- the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected beat, not the default 'Showing 7 stories'.
Do not damage the existing Cinder & Rail masthead, Green Line showcase hero, Editors Picks grid, the seven story cards, local images, the article page, or navigation; keep the branding on every page.
design_constraints: Keep the Cinder & Rail editorial visual language: white story cards, the #c72727 red primary accent, the #f99500 amber secondary accent, the dark #333 masthead/footer, condensed narrow headline type, sticky masthead.
Do not replace the newsroom, the reader-signal filter, or the pages with a new app shell, framework, external design system, or unrelated layout.
Do not remove the reader-signal filter panel, the four beat chips, the shared footer rail, the story cards, the hero, the navigation, or the filter script.
Do not add npm dependencies, remote scripts, remote fonts, remote images, generated build outputs, or unrelated file churn.
The filter strip and rail must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, and must render in the Cinder & Rail red/charcoal editorial palette.
state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home, and mobile_home verify the original newsroom shell and repaired responsive layout across breakpoints.
desktop_signal_component and mobile_signal_component verify the new filter component is visible above the Editors Picks grid.
desktop_transit_filter and mobile_transit_filter click Transit and verify the focused three-story status readout and filtered card state.
desktop_infrastructure_filter clicks Infrastructure and verifies the second focused-status filter state.
desktop_all_reset clicks a focused state then All stories and returns to the full seven-story view.
desktop_cards_regression verifies the original Editors Picks cards, images, and read-more links remain present after the component extension.
desktop_about, desktop_article, and mobile_about verify the shared reader-signal rail appears in the footer of the secondary pages.

change_completion: The reader-signal filter panel and its four beat chips appear above the Editors Picks grid on the home page.
The shared 'Reader signal rail' appears in the footer of all three pages (home, about, article).
On mobile the home page has no horizontal overflow after the responsive layout.
content_asset_continuity: The story cards stay grounded in the repo's local imagery (Green Line platform, signal cabinets, harbour ferry); no external or placeholder media.
The Cinder & Rail masthead, hero, Editors Picks cards, and navigation are preserved.
design_consistency: The filter strip and shared rail keep the Cinder & Rail red/charcoal editorial style and are visually faithful to the reference.
The same reader-signal component is consistent across all three pages; the hero, cards, and masthead remain recognizable.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a beat chip updates the 'Showing N stories' status readout to the selected beat (the post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
The All stories reset restores the full seven-story view and status.
regression: Home, about, and article pages retain the Cinder & Rail branding, nav labels, and imagery.
No new dependency, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced.
responsive: The home page has no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile states.
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow.

scoring_notes: A correct patch extends the Editors Picks area with a real beat filter and a shared footer rail, plus a targeted responsive layout so the mobile home page does not overflow. Static labels without click behaviour, filters that leave the status readout stale after the click, a rail added to only the home page, a fixed-width non-wrapping chip row that overflows on mobile, a collapsed off-palette restyle, replaced local images, removed hero/cards/read-more links, new dependencies, or remote media should fail completion, regression, responsive, visual, interaction, cross-page, asset, or source checks.
author_notes: Slot 214 targets the leogodoyllg News-Website-Template repository (rebranded Cinder & Rail transit newsroom) for editorial_blog / Regression Continuity / extend_interaction / component / L4. The reader-signal filter and the shared footer rail reuse the repo's existing local article imagery (ent1.jpg, tech1.jpg, sports1.jpg, tech2.jpg) and the red/charcoal editorial palette. The task carries four orthogonal levers: a cross-page dom_assertions invariant (the rail on every page), a visual_regression faithful-restyle check on the filter panel, an interaction_assertions terminal-state readout check, and a mobile no_horizontal_overflow responsive repair, each of which independently discriminates a shallow solution.
